jordi (Growth): Quick one — I'm planning to relocate from Brooklyn, NY to Toronto, ON (Canada) on 2026-08-01. I'm still Redwood-engaged full time. How does this affect the $60 WFH stipend, payroll (US -> Canada), benefits eligibility, and equity tax withholding?
nina (People Ops): Congrats on the move! :canada: Short version: cross-border moves are more complex. Stipend: we usually continue stipend for remote employees, but currency/expense treatment may differ. Payroll: we may need to move you to our Canada payroll provider (EOR) or explore cross-border payroll; Legal & Payroll must confirm. Benefits: some US plans don't cover Canada, so you might be shifted to local benefits or offered an alternative. Equity/tax: Legal will advise re: withholding on stock exercises/grants.
ivan (Payroll): Adding detail: if we transfer payroll to a Canadian payroll vendor, you'll be paid in CAD and Canadian payroll taxes will apply. If we stay on US payroll temporarily, you'll have dual-tax implications and may need a Canadian tax registration for employer withholding. We need the exact move date and work authorization status.
jordi (Growth): I have PR and Canadian SIN. Move date 2026-08-01. I want to stay on Redwood payroll if possible and keep stock option vesting unchanged.
maria (Legal): With Canadian PR and SIN it's straightforward to put you on Canadian payroll. A few legal notes: 1) Employment agreement may need a local addendum. 2) Stock option taxation on exercise can be subject to Canadian withholding; consult our equity counsel. 3) Cross-border vesting continues but tax residency changes the tax treatment. We'll loop in equity counsel for specific scenarios.
nina (People Ops): Action items for you: 1) Submit Location Change form and upload proof (lease, utility, or SIN copy) in HR portal. 2) Fill out the 'International Move' checklist that People Ops will DM. 3) Talk to your manager + People Ops to confirm relocation assistance eligibility (different approval flow).
jordi (Growth): About the WFH stipend — will it be converted to CAD or replaced with a local allowance?
ivan (Payroll): Typically we convert stipend to an equivalent monthly amount in the local currency based on a standard conversion policy and local benefits. For Canada we apply cost-of-living and payroll feasibility — tentatively CAD $80/mo equivalent (subject to approval). We'll confirm exact conversion and taxation (might be taxable as income locally).
maria (Legal): Also consider benefits network: if you move to Canadian payroll, you'll be on local benefits which may have different coverage and enrollment windows. Moving countries usually counts as a qualifying life event for benefits but plan availability differs.
hris-bot: HRIS action required: please update Profile > Work Location and upload proof documents. Create ticket #INTL-2026-881 when completed for cross-border payroll setup.
nina (People Ops): We'll schedule a quick call with Payroll + Legal to review equity withholding, payroll timing, and stipend currency. For timeline: aim to submit the forms 2 weeks before move to avoid payroll cutoff issues.
jordi (Growth): Thanks — I'll submit forms today. Appreciate the call.
ivan (Payroll): Ticket #PAY-2026-391 opened to evaluate payroll transfer, stipend conversion, and withholding. ETA: 3-5 business days for initial assessment.
maria (Legal): We'll follow up on equity tax specifics — please avoid exercising options until we confirm withholding approach to prevent surprises.
nina (People Ops): Noted. I'll DM the checklist and book the triage call. Welcome to Canada in advance! :maple_leaf:
